rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says that because a trusted debtor may turn out dishonest, God urges anyone who knows the transaction to help preserve the creditor’s right by testifying, whether or not the creditor knows of the testimony.
rows.anchor: ذلك الإنسان إلى أن يسعى في إحياء ذلك الحق

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report supports Al-Qaffal’s reading: the best witness is one who testifies before being asked.
rows.anchor: خير الشهود من شهد قبل أن يستشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes concealing testimony to mean denying knowledge of the event, as in the denial concerning Abraham’s family in 2:140.
rows.anchor: أن ينكر العلم بتلك الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is withholding testimony when needed; as already stated at 2:282, refusal can defeat a Muslim’s property right and is gravely warned against.
rows.anchor: في كتمان الشهادة والامتناع من أدائها عند الحاجة إلى إقامتها

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report says ʿUmar taught a Bedouin that athīm in the phrase about the tree of Zaqqūm means a wicked person, not an orphan.
rows.anchor: روي أن عمر كان يعلم أعرابيا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf parses āthim as the predicate of inna and qalbuhu as its nominative agent, equivalent to saying that his heart sins.
rows.anchor: آثم خبر إن وقلبه رفع بآثم على الفاعلية كأنه قيل فإنه يأثم قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with qalbahu in the accusative parallels safiha nafsahu in 2:130.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { قلبه } بالفتح كقوله { سفه نفسه }

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads qalbuhu Allāh, explaining the construction as God making the heart sinful.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة { قلبه والله } أي جعله آثما

rows.speaker: كثير من المتكلمين
rows.claim: Many theologians argue that the heart is the acting, knowing, commanded, and prohibited subject; they infer this from God attributing sin to the heart here.
rows.anchor: إن الفاعل والعارف والمأمور والمنهي هو القلب

rows.speaker: من خالف في هذا القول
rows.claim: Opponents answer that an act can be attributed to a body part because that organ supplies its chief enabling cause, as in saying the eye saw or ear heard.
rows.anchor: إضافة الفعل إلى جزء من أجزاء البدن إنما يكون لأجل أن أعظم أسباب الإعانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since bodily acts follow the heart’s motives and inclinations, the sin is attributed to the heart in this verse.
rows.anchor: أفعال الجوارح تابعة لأفعال القلوب ومتولدة مما يحدث في القلوب من الدواعي والصوارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge of actions and inner thoughts warns against concealing testimony: the accountable person knows every deed will be judged and recompensed; the following verse is cited.
rows.anchor: إذا علم أنه لا يعزب عن علم الله ضمير قلبه كان خائفا حذرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the threat, God promises the God-fearing a reception; nuzul is what is prepared for a guest, and taqwa includes avoiding prohibitions and neglecting no commands.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر الوعيد أتبعه بالوعد بالنزل

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of the author’s colleagues use this verse to argue for seeing God: if all Paradise is the believers’ reception, it must include the vision as a gift; 18:107 is analogous.
rows.anchor: احتج بعض أصحابنا بهذه الآية على الرؤية لأنه لما كانت الجنة بكليتها نزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzulan may be an accusative circumstantial qualifier of gardens, licensed by their description, with the governing element the lām.
rows.anchor: نصب على الحال من { جنات } لتخصيصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nuzulan is an emphatic verbal noun: their abiding in Paradise means their being settled or descending there.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى مصدر مؤكد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses nuzulan as an accusative specification, like describing something as a gift, sale, or charity.
rows.anchor: هو نصب على التفسير كما تقول

rows.speaker: مسلمة بن محارب والأعمش
rows.claim: Muslimah ibn Muḥārib and al-Aʿmash read nuzul with a still zāy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن محارب والأعمش { نزلا } بسكون الزاي

rows.speaker: يزيد بن القعقاع
rows.claim: Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ reads lakin with a doubled kāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن القعقاع { لكن الذين اتقوا } بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is with God is abundant and enduring, better for the righteous than the transitory little enjoyed by the wicked.
rows.anchor: مما يتقلب فيه الفجار من القليل الزائل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر وقتادة
rows.claim: One reported occasion is the death of the Negus: the Prophet prayed over him, and hypocrites objected that he prayed for a Christian he had never seen.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وجابر وقتادة : نزلت في النجاشي حين مات

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd say the verse was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وابن زيد : نزلت في عبدالله بن سلام وأصحابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report identifies forty people from Najrān, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and eight from Rome who had followed Jesus and then accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في أربعين من أهل نجران

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the verse concerns all believing People of Scripture; al-Rāzī prefers this general reading because it contrasts their reward with the punishment of the disbelievers just mentioned.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : نزلت في مؤمني أهل الكتاب كلهم ، وهذا هو الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers described first have faith in God, then in what was revealed to Muḥammad, and then in revelation given to earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: أولها : الايمان بالله ، وثانيها : الايمان بما أنزل الله على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humility is a circumstantial qualifier attached to the subject of يؤمن, since من يؤمن has a collective sense.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : كونهم خاشعين لله وهو حال من فاعل { يؤمن } لأن { من يؤمن } في معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not trade God’s signs for a small price, unlike People of Scripture who concealed the Messenger’s identity and the truth of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا كما يفعله أهل الكتاب ممن كان يكتم أمر الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is with their Lord, and God’s swift reckoning reflects His knowledge of every fact and of each person’s due reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: والفائدة في كونه سريع الحساب كونه عالما بجميع المعلومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s closing verse gathers its teachings: the foundations of faith include monotheism, divine justice, prophethood, and resurrection, while its practical rulings include pilgrimage and jihad.
rows.anchor: أنواعا كثيرة من علوم الأصول والفروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human circumstances are individual or shared: patience applies to what concerns oneself, while steadfastly bearing what occurs with others is muṣābara.
rows.anchor: منها ما يتعلق به وحده ، ومنها ما يكون مشتركا بينه وبين غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience includes bearing the intellectual work of proving monotheism, justice, prophethood, and resurrection and answering opponents’ doubts.
rows.anchor: أن يصبر على مشقة النظر والاستدلال في معرفة التوحيد والعدل والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience also means enduring the difficulty of performing obligatory and recommended acts.
rows.anchor: أن يصبر على مشقة أداء الواجبات والمندوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience includes bearing the difficulty of avoiding prohibited acts.
rows.anchor: أن يصبر على مشقة الاحتراز عن المنهيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also covers worldly trials and afflictions, including illness, poverty, drought, and fear.
rows.anchor: الصبر على شدائد الدنيا وآفاتها من المرض والفقر والقحط والخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muṣābara includes enduring bad conduct by family, neighbors, and relatives, and refraining from retaliation; the author cites 7:199 and 25:72.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه تحمل الاخلاق الردية من أهل البيت والجيران والأقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It includes preferring others over oneself, linked to 59:9.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه الايثار على الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It includes forgiving someone who wronged you, since forgiving is nearer to God-consciousness (2:237).
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه العفو عمن ظلمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It includes enjoining right and forbidding wrong, jihad despite exposure to harm, and persevering with opponents while resolving their doubts and removing falsehood from their hearts.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Appetitive desire, anger, and greed impel people away from patience; lifelong struggle to master these blameworthy traits is necessary for patience and muṣābara.
rows.anchor: فيه أخلاقا ذميمة تحمل على أضدادها وهي الشهوة والغضب والحرص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since action arises from inner faculties, murābaṭa means struggling against the powers that generate blameworthy deeds; taqwa repels their prompting, and success is the goal that motivates it.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو المراد بالمرابطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the verse compresses spiritual wisdom and completes the surah’s treatment of foundational beliefs and practical duties.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية التي هي خاتمة لهذه السورة مشتملة على كنوز الحكم والاسرار الروحانية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to remain patient in religion despite poverty and hunger, and to stand firm against the enemy despite the defeat at Uḥud.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : اصبروا على دينكم ولا تتركوه بسبب الفقر والجوع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets the commands as patience alongside the Prophet and steadfastness against the enemy, so Muslims should outlast them.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : اصبروا مع نبيكم وصابروا عدوكم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the many duties discussed in the surah call for patience, while its repeated encouragement of jihad calls for steadfastness against enemies.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم : لما كثرت تكاليف الله في هذه السورة أمرهم بالصبر عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of murābaṭa is stationing tethered horses at frontier posts, with both sides ready to fight; the author links this to 8:60.
rows.anchor: أنه عبارة عن أن يربط هؤلاء خيلهم في الثغور ويربط أولئك خيلهم أيضا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says a day and night stationed in God’s cause equals a month of fasting and prayer, without breaking the fast or leaving prayer except for need.
rows.anchor: من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان مثل صيام شهر وقيامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is waiting for one prayer after another.
rows.anchor: أن معنى المرابطة انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abū Salama ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says there was no campaign requiring frontier duty in the Prophet’s time, so the verse concerned waiting for the next prayer.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن أبي سلمة عبد الرحمن أنه قال : لم يكن في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غزو

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra describes waiting for prayer after prayer and calls this murābaṭa three times.
rows.anchor: ما روي من حديث أبي هريرة حين ذكر انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة ثم قال : ( فذلكم الرباط ) ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can include both frontier service and waiting for prayer: ribāṭ comes from binding, and one may bind one’s heart to what one patiently undertakes.
rows.anchor: يمكن حمل اللفظ على الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpreters define ribāṭ as persistence and staying firm, which also returns to patience and self-discipline; this steadiness may be in jihad or in prayer.
rows.anchor: الرباط هو اللزوم والثبات ، وهذا المعنى أيضا راجع إلى ما ذكرناه من الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī records that he completed the commentary on this surah on Thursday, the first of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir 595 AH.
rows.anchor: تم تفسير هذه السورة بفضل الله وإحسانه يوم الخميس أول ربيع الآخر سنة خمس وتسعين وخمسمائة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Mujāhid interpret good speech as a kindly promise of benevolence and maintaining kinship.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج ومجاهد : انه العدة الجميلة من البر والصلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives examples of promising the ward a fitting share if a journey yields profit or a campaign yields booty.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : هو مثل أن يقول : اذا ربحت في سفرتي هذه فعلت بك ما انت أهله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets good speech as supplication, such as asking God to grant health and bless the other person.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : انه الدعاء مثل أن يقول : عافانا الله وإياك بارك الله فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More generally, recognized good is any speech or action that reassures and pleases people, while wrong is what they reject, dislike, and recoil from.
rows.anchor: كل ما سكنت اليه النفوس وأحبته من قول وعمل فهو معروف وكل ما أنكرته وكرهته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says guardians should teach wards religion, including knowledge and practice, while feeding and clothing them.
rows.anchor: علموهم مع إطعامكم وكسوتكم إياهم أمر دينهم مما يتعلق بالعلم والعمل

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl’s preferred explanation: tell a child that the wealth belongs to them, that the guardian only keeps it, and that it will be returned at maturity; for a foolish ward, advise against waste, encourage prayer, and warn of future poverty.
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله القول المعروف / هو أنه ان كان المولى عليه صبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because 4:2 ordered guardians to hand over orphan property, this verse specifies when: both puberty and discerned sound judgment must be established before delivery.
rows.anchor: أمر من قبل بدفع مال اليتيم اليه بقوله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds that a discerning child’s transactions with the guardian’s permission are valid; he reads the testing command as allowing supervised buying and selling before puberty.
rows.anchor: تصرفات الصبي العاقل المميز باذن الولي صحيحة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds such transactions invalid. Al-Rāzī sides with him: testing can mean observing transactions done by the guardian and asking the child to assess them, or letting the child handle an item while the guardian ratifies the sale.
rows.anchor: أجاب الشافعي رضي الله عنه بأن قال : ليس المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the age of marriage means puberty, identified by emission, as in 24:59; it is when legal accountability and penalties begin, and the label refers to the emission involved in intercourse.
rows.anchor: المراد من بلوغ النكاح هو الاحتلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Puberty has five signs: wet dream, a specified age, and coarse pubic hair for both sexes; menstruation and pregnancy are further signs for women.
rows.anchor: للبلوغ علامات خمسة : منها ثلاثة مشتركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īnās means knowing or, according to another gloss, seeing; its linguistic root is vision, as in the reference to seeing a fire at 28:29.
rows.anchor: وأصل الايناس في اللغة الابصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required judgment concerns financial competence: the ward can manage property, avoid waste, and resist being deceived.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يعلم أنه مصلح لما له حتى لا يقع منه إسراف

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires religious uprightness as well as financial competence, whereas Abū Ḥanīfa does not; al-Rāzī prefers al-Shāfiʿī because rushd means attaining good, contrasts with error (2:256), and is denied of sinful Adam and Pharaoh (20:121; 11:97).
rows.anchor: فعند الشافعي رضي الله عنه لا بد منه ، وعند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement over religious uprightness matters because al-Shāfiʿī places a sinful person under legal restraint, while Abū Ḥanīfa does not.
rows.anchor: الشافعي رحمه الله يرى الحجر على الفاسق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The jurists agree that an adolescent who is not financially sound does not receive the estate; Abū Ḥanīfa releases it at twenty-five regardless of demonstrated judgment, after puberty at eighteen plus seven years for changing maturity, invoking the prayer training age of seven.
rows.anchor: ثم عند أبي حنيفة لا يدفع اليه ماله حتى يبلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Yūsuf, and Muḥammad say the estate is withheld indefinitely until sound judgment is actually observed.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : لا يدفع إليه أبدا إلا بايناس الرشد

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that an indefinite noun rushd requires only some rationality, so once age twenty-five arrives the verse’s condition is met.
rows.anchor: احتج أبو بكر الرازي لأبي حنيفة بهذه الآية فقال : لا شك أن اسم الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that argument: the context makes financial stewardship the required judgment; otherwise the syntax loses coherence, and anyone still unable to protect property at twenty-five remains like a child and must not receive it.
rows.anchor: المراد ابتلاؤهم فيما يتعلق بمصالح حفظ المال

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: If someone first reaches sound judgment and later becomes foolish, al-Shāfiʿī would restrain him, while Abū Ḥanīfa would not; al-Rāzī supports restraint by analogy with the still-unfit minor whose property is preserved for future need.
rows.anchor: إذا بلغ رشيدا ثم تغير وصار سفيها حجر عليه عند الشافعي ولا يحجر عليه عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the indefinite rushd may mean financial and commercial sound judgment specifically, or may mean any discernible sign of it without awaiting complete maturity.
rows.anchor: الفائدة في تنكير الرشد التنبيه على ان المعتبر هو الرشد في التصرف والتجارة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads fa-in aḥsastum, meaning fa-in aḥsastum/perceived; a cited line witnesses the form aḥsana bihi.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن مسعود فان أحستم ، بمعنى أحسستم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rushd is also read with two fatḥas or with two ḍammas.
rows.anchor: وقرىء رشدا بفتحتين ورشدا بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once puberty and discerned judgment are both present, guardians must hand over the property; no separate complete-intellect condition is stated because judgment already entails more than basic reason.
rows.anchor: عند حصول الشرطين أعني البلوغ وإيناس الرشد يجب دفع المال اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians must not consume the property wastefully or hasten to spend it before the orphans grow up and reclaim it; the phrase describes their waste and haste.
rows.anchor: مسرفين ومبادرين كبرهم أو لاسرافكم ومبادرتكم كبرهم تفرطون في إنفاقها

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains istaʿaffa and ʿaffa as refraining and abstaining.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : استعف عن الشيء وعف اذا امتنع منه وتركه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says istaʿaffa is more emphatic than ʿaffa, as if one actively seeks greater chastity.
rows.anchor: استعف أبلغ من عف كأنه طالب زيادة العفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One legal view allows a needy guardian to use from the ward’s wealth what is needed and a fair amount for the work; the verse’s contrast and its distinction between unjust and non-unjust consumption support this allowance.
rows.anchor: أن له أن يأخذ بقدر ما يحتاج اليه من مال اليتيم وبقدر أجر عمله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether he could use an orphan’s wealth; the reply permits fair use without accumulating wealth or protecting one’s own property with it, and allows discipline as with one’s child.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن رجلا قال له : ان تحت حجري يتيما أآكل من ماله ؟ قال : بالمعروف

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In a letter to ʿAmmār, Ibn Masʿūd, and ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf, ʿUmar assigns shares from public funds and compares their role to a guardian of an orphan.
rows.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كتب إلى عمار وابن مسعود وعثمان بن حنيف : سلام عليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās permits a guardian to drink an orphan’s camel milk if he tends and waters the animal, while avoiding harm to its young or excessive milking.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن ولي يتيم قال له : أفأشرب من لبن إبله ؟ قال : إن كنت تبغي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the guardian may eat moderately by sharing in their work but should not wear even a turban beyond that allowance.
rows.anchor: يضرب بيده مع أيديهم فليأكل بالمعروف ولا يلبس عمامة فما فوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardianship work may merit compensation by analogy with collectors of charity, who receive a designated share.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يتمكن من أن يأكل من ماله بقدر عمله قياسا على الساعي في أخذ الصدقات

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبو العالية
rows.claim: A second view allows a poor guardian to borrow only what is needed and repay when able; if death comes before repayment despite inability, nothing is owed. This is attributed to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and most reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وأبي العالية ، وأكثر الروايات عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو العالية وغيره
rows.claim: Some restrict borrowing to principal assets such as gold and silver, while allowing harmless use of livestock milk, servants, and riding animals.
rows.anchor: خص هذا الاقراض بأصول الأموال من الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who allow this use reason from the command to return the orphan’s property, taking that to govern the assets themselves.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا بأن الله تعالى قال : { فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم }

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī reports his school’s view that guardians may take nothing from the orphan, whether as a loan or outright and whether rich or poor; he cites 4:2, 4:10, 4:127, and 2:188 as decisive texts against the possibly ambiguous permission here.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي : الذي نعرفه من مذهب أصحابنا أنه لا يأخذ على سبيل القرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the argument: 4:2 is general while this verse is specific, and the other prohibitions only apply if moderate guardian use is already proved unjust, which is the very issue disputed.
rows.anchor: أما قوله : { وءاتوا اليتامى أموالهم } فهو عام وهذه الآية التي نحن فيها خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees that witnesses should preferably attest when a guardian hands over an adult orphan’s property: this deters a false claim by the recipient, lets the guardian defend against such a claim, and demonstrates the guardian’s integrity.
rows.anchor: الأمة مجمعة على أن الوصي إذا دفع المال إلى اليتيم بعد صيرورته بالغا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed a person who found lost property to bring upright witnesses and neither hide nor lose it, so that the finder’s trustworthiness is evident.
rows.anchor: من وجد لقطة فليشهد ذوي عدل ولا يكتم ولا يغيب

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī do not accept the guardian’s bare claim that he delivered the property or spent it on the ward; Abū Ḥanīfa and his associates do accept it.
rows.anchor: قال مالك والشافعي : لا يصدق ، وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه : يصدق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats the command to call witnesses as obligatory and argues that the guardian is entrusted by religious law, not personally by the orphan.
rows.anchor: فإن قوله : { فأشهدوا عليهم } أمر ، وظاهر الأمر الوجوب ، وأيضا قال الشافعي : القيم غير مؤتمن من جهة اليتيم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that if the guardian is not believed because the orphan did not entrust him, the same should apply to a judge or father, and even to property both parties admit was lost.
rows.anchor: لو كان ما ذكره علة لنفي التصديق لوجب أن لا يصدق القاضي إذا قال لليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the analogies: distrust of a judge would create endless appeals; a father has greater compassion than a stranger; a non-negligent accidental loss must be accepted or guardianship would fail, unlike witnessed delivery.
rows.anchor: القاضي حاكم فيجب إزالة التهمة عنه ليصير قضاؤه نافذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding warning against consuming wealth hastily before the orphan grows up shows why suspicion of guardians is well-founded and strengthens the case for witnessing delivery.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على جريان العادة بكثرة إقدام الولي على ظلم الايتام والصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing protects the orphan from injustice and short delivery because the guardian cannot convincingly claim to have transferred the assets without witnesses; al-Rāzī says both the command’s wording and its purpose require it.
rows.anchor: إذا كان لا يتمكن من ادعاء دفع المال اليه إلا عند حضور الشاهد ، صار ذلك مانعا له من الظلم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that since a guardian is entrusted with safekeeping, he should be believed when returning the property just as a deposit holder is.
rows.anchor: فهو بمنزلة الودائع والمضاربات ، فوجب أن يكون مصدقا على الرد كما يصدق على رد الوديعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that al-Shāfiʿī already explained the difference from ordinary deposits and rejects the opposing analogy as a weak imagined piece of jurisprudence that ignores scripture.
rows.anchor: أما الفرق بين هذه الصورة وصورة الوديعة فقد ذكره الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري والأزهري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī and al-Azharī say ḥasīb can mean one who reckons and calls to account, or one who suffices; both meanings suit this warning.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون الحسيب بمعنى المحاسب ، وأن يكون بمعنى الكافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns the guardian that God knows inward and outward intentions, ensuring complete trustworthiness until the orphan receives the property.
rows.anchor: هذا وعيد لولي اليتيم وإعلام له أنه تعالى يعلم باطنه كما يعلم ظاهره

rows.speaker: الواحدي عن الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī transmits from al-Zajjāj that the bāʾ in wa-kafā bi-llāh and wa-kafā bi-rabbika is redundant; ḥasīban is accusative as a circumstantial expression meaning reckoning or sufficiency.
rows.anchor: أن الباء في قوله : { وكفى بالله } { وكفى بربك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse portrays two losses for deniers of resurrection: they squandered bodily and intellectual faculties meant to gain enduring knowledge and virtue on transient pleasure, losing both their capital and supposed profit.
rows.anchor: أعطاه العقل والتفكر أجل أن يتوصل باستعمال هذه الآلات والأدوات إلى تحصيل المعارف الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This loss applies to deniers who believe present bodily pleasure is the highest happiness; believers expect resurrection and prepare provisions for the return, so they are not deceived by temporary goods.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخسران إنما يحصل لمن كان منكرا للبعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other loss is that unbelievers prepare no provisions or detachment from worldly ties; after death they are strangers in the spiritual realm, grieving both their lack of preparation and separation from earthly pleasures.
rows.anchor: فإذا مات بقي كالغريب في عالم الروحانيات ، وكالمنقطع عن أحبابه وأقاربه الذين كانوا في عالم الجسمانيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lament about neglect points to failing to prepare for reward, while carrying loads on their backs points to having earned punishment.
rows.anchor: فالأول : هو المراد من قوله { قالوا يأبانا * ياحسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها } والثاني : هو المراد من قوله { وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss means forfeiting immense reward and receiving immense punishment; meeting God refers to denying resurrection, and the expression is apt because only God controls benefit, harm, elevation, and abasement at Judgment.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الذين أنكروا البعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Until marks the endpoint of their denial, not of their loss, since loss has no endpoint: they persisted in denial until the sudden Hour made their regret appear.
rows.anchor: كلمة ( حتى ) غاية لقوله { كذبوا } لا لقوله { قد خسر } لأن خسرانهم لا غاية له

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that death is an entry into the states and preliminaries of the afterlife, so it is treated as part of the Hour; a prophetic saying states that whoever dies has had his Hour established.
rows.anchor: من مات فقد قامت قيامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is named either for the speed of reckoning or because it arrives suddenly at an unknown time; baghtatan can be a circumstantial adverb or an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الساعة هي الوقت الذي تقوم القيامة سميت ساعة لأنها تفجأ الناس في ساعة لا يعلمها أحد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says calling out يا حسرتنا alerts people to the regret awaiting them; Arabs intensify such events by addressing them directly, as in 36:30, 39:56, 11:72, and 12:84.
rows.anchor: أن النداء للحسرة ، والمراد منه تنبيه المخاطبين وهو قول الزجاج

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayhi takes regret itself as the addressee: the phrase means, in effect, O regret, come, for this is your time.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن المنادى هو نفس الحسرة على معنى : أن هذا وقتك فاحضري وهو قول سيبويه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines farraṭtu fī al-shayʾ as neglecting or wasting it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة يقال : فرطت في الشيء أي ضيعته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives farraṭnā from advancing or letting something go ahead, so neglect is bringing failure forward.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : فرطنا أي قدمنا العجز جعله من قولهم فرط فلان إذا سبق وتقدم

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī summarizes al-Zajjāj’s account as neglect consisting in putting shortcoming first.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : فالتفريط عنده تقديم التقصير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the pronoun in fīhā to refer to worldly life, though it was not explicitly mentioned; reason identifies it as the place of neglect.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في الدنيا والسؤال عليه أنه لم يجر للدنيا ذكر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the pronoun to refer to the Hour: they regret failing to prepare provisions for it.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن المراد يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا في الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view refers the pronoun to the implied deeds in ما فرطنا, namely the actions and acts of worship they neglected.
rows.anchor: أن تعود الكناية إلى معنى ما في قوله { ما فرطنا } أي حسرتنا على الأعمال والطاعات التي فرطنا فيها

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the pronoun refers to the transaction implied by خسِروا: their lament concerns the bargain they lost.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن جرير الطبري : الكناية تعود إلى الصفقة لأنه تعالى لما ذكر الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failing to prepare for reward and earning grounds for severe punishment together constitute the ultimate loss.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم لم يحصلوا لأنفسهم ما به يستحقون الثواب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the loads as sins and errors; the root sense of a burden explains why sins are called weights.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الأوزار الآثام والخطايا قال أهل اللغة الوزر الثقل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda illustrates the root w-z-r with carrying goods in a garment, the burdens of war, and a ruler’s minister carrying the weight of delegated administration.
rows.anchor: يقال للرجل إذا بسط ثوبه فجعل فيه المتاع أحمل وزرك وأوزار الحرب أثقالها من السلاح

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that people carry the weight of their sins.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : وهم يحملون أوزارهم أي يحملون ثقل ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: A report attributed to Qatāda and al-Suddī says righteous or corrupt deeds meet their owners after resurrection as a beautiful pleasant-smelling or ugly foul-smelling mount, and each carries or is carried by that deed; 19:85 is cited.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة والسدي .

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the weight metaphorically: the punishment of their sins is painful and burdensome.
rows.anchor: الثقل كما يذكر في المنقول ، فقد يذكر أيضا في الحال والصفة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say their sins remain inseparable from them, as in saying that someone’s memory stands constantly before one’s eyes.
rows.anchor: معنى قوله { وهم يحملون أوزارهم } أي لا تزايلهم أوزارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase means how evil is what they bear; detailed treatment of the expression is deferred to the discussion of 4:22.
rows.anchor: { ألا ساء ما يزرون } والمعنى بئس الشيء الذي يزرونه أي يحملونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people first appealed to ancestral imitation and rejected the notion of one God, as in 43:23 and 38:5; they also threatened that their idols would afflict him, like Hūd’s people in 11:54.
rows.anchor: أوردوا عليه حججا على صحة أقوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham answers that sound proof has given him guidance, so their defective arguments and false words deserve no consideration.
rows.anchor: يعني لما ثبت بالدليل الموجب للهداية واليقين صحة قولي ، فكيف يلتفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects fear of idols because fear properly concerns an agent able to cause benefit or harm, while idols are inert and powerless.
rows.anchor: والأصنام جمادات لا تقدر ولا قدرة لها على النفع والضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if talismans appear to have effects, their effects come from the stars, whose powers God created; ultimate fear and hope therefore belong to God.
rows.anchor: وقد دللنا على أن قوى الكواكب على التأثيرات إنما يحصل من خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception except if my Lord wills may mean that Abraham sins and is punished, faces worldly trials and loss of some accustomed blessings, or that God revives and empowers the idols; the wording can bear all three.
rows.anchor: واللفظ يحتمل كل هذه الوجوه ، وحاصل الأمر أنه لا يبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham anticipates future misfortunes so foolish people will not mistake them for punishment caused by his rejection of idols.
rows.anchor: ذكر إبراهيم عليه السلام ذلك حتى لو أنه حدث به شيء من المكاره لم يحمل على هذا السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses all knowledge and acts only with wisdom and benefit; any worldly hardship would reflect what God knows best, not punishment for challenging the idols.
rows.anchor: { وسع ربى كل شىء علما } يعني أنه علام الغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should recognize that denying partners to God and affirming monotheism do not bring punishment or make one deserve it.
rows.anchor: نفي الشركاء والأضداد والأنداد عن الله تعالى لا يوجب حلول العقاب

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read ataḥājjūnī with a light nūn by deleting one of the two; other readers retain the doubled nūn through assimilation.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر { أتحاجونى } خفيفة النون على حذف أحد النونين

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir retain the yāʾ in hadānī, while the other readers omit it for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر { هدانى } بإثبات الياء على الأصل والباقون بحذفها للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Debate over God merits praise when it establishes true religion, as Abraham’s argument does (6:83), and blame when it establishes falsehood; Qur’anic and hadith censure of disputation concerns false doctrine.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بين هذين البابين إلا أن المحاجة في تقرير الدين الحق توجب أعظم أنواح المدح والثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham continues his answer: he does not fear powerless idols, while his opponents fail to fear the greater sin of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : وكيف أخاف الأصنام التي لا قدرة لها على النفع والضر ، وأنتم لا تخافون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God not sending authority either implies that no proof for shirk can exist, as in 23:117, or that no revealed command authorizes worshipping images, though it is not rationally impossible to direct prayer toward them.
rows.anchor: كناية عن امتناع وجود الحجة والسلطان في مثل هذه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking which group deserves security avoids Abraham’s self-praise; he shifts from asking which of us to asking which of the two parties, idolaters or monotheists.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : فأينا أحق بالأمن أنا أم أنتم ؟ احترازا من تزكية نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s answer defines full security through faith and freedom from wrongdoing, representing perfected theoretical and practical capacities.
rows.anchor: أولهما : الإيمان وهو كمال القوة النظرية . وثانيهما : { ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } وهو كمال القوة العملية

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s theological school argues that faith remains compatible with major sin: if avoiding all wrongdoing were already part of faith, adding it as a separate condition would be pointless.
rows.anchor: لو كان ترك الظلم أحد أجزاء مسمى الإيمان لكان هذا التقييد عبثا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that security requires both faith and absence of wrongdoing, so the sinner cannot have security and is subject to the threat of punishment.
rows.anchor: فوجب أن لا يحصل الأمن للفاسق وذلك يوجب حصول الوعيد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting the unbelievers’ false claims about what God prohibited, the verse states the actual prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أردفه تعالى ببيان الأشياء التي حرمها عليهم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says taʿāl is originally a call from someone higher to someone below, but it became a general invitation.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ( تعال ) من الخاص الذي صار عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object in mā ḥarrama rabbukum may be governed by atlu, meaning recite what He prohibited, or by ḥarrama, meaning recite the things He prohibited you.
rows.anchor: وفي ناصبه وجهان : الأول : أنه منصوب بقوله : { اتل } والتقدير : أتل الذي حرمه عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent problem is that the list under what God prohibited includes avoiding shirk and doing good to parents, which are obligations rather than prohibitions.
rows.anchor: لأن ترك الشرك والإحسان بالوالدين واجب ، لا محرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer understands taḥrīm as God’s clearly fixed and delineated prescription, removing the objection about obligatory acts in the list.
rows.anchor: المراد من التحريم أن يجعل له حريما معينا ، وذلك بأن بينه بيانا مضبوطا معينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer changes the clause boundary: the sentence may end at recite what God prohibited, after which a new clause begins with you must not associate, or it may end after prohibited you and begin with ألا تشركوا as lialla.
rows.anchor: أن الكلام تم وانقطع عند قوله { أتل ما حرم ربكم } ثم ابتدأ فقال : { عليكم أن * لا * تشركوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer takes أن as explanatory, effectively saying: recite what God prohibited, namely, do not associate anything with Him.
rows.anchor: أن تكون ( أن ) / في قوله : { أن لا * تشركوا } مفسرة بمعنى : أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt then raises an unresolved objection: because kindness to parents is coordinated with the explanatory prohibition of shirk, the same reading appears to make parental kindness forbidden.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : فقوله : { وبالوالدين إحسانا } معطوف على قوله : { أن لا * تشركوا به شيئا }
